description: A purchase document: embedded line items (snapshotted, see commerce.line-item), a totals block, shipping/billing addresses, and two independent lifecycle tracks (status, fulfillmentStatus). Has no id property -- consumers key orders in their own systems. Every monetary amount in this document, including inside each line item, is assumed to share one currency; this schema cannot cross-check that.

$kind.description: Optional self-identifier (cf. GraphQL __typename). Omit when the enclosing schema already names the role -- a value held under a property literally named order is unambiguously an order without needing $kind. Include only when this object might appear untyped outside its normal context.

billingAddress.description: Address associated with payment/billing for this order. Optional; may differ from shippingAddress.

customerId.description: Opaque id of the customer who placed the order, keyed in the consumer's own system. This schema has no customer entity -- customer/person/org modeling is out of scope for this launch catalog.

discountTotal.description: Order-level discount applied on top of subtotal, distinct from any per-row discountAmount already reflected in each line item's own amount. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

externalReferences.description: Links to corresponding records in foreign systems, e.g. Stripe or Shopify -- see external-reference for shape and validation. Replaces ad-hoc *Id fields scattered across schemas with one uniform array.

fulfillmentStatus.description: Fulfillment lifecycle, independent of status -- an order can be completed but only partially fulfilled (e.g. a backorder). Absent means unfulfilled. Returns and exchanges are deliberately deferred out of this launch catalog: the money side of a return lives on billing.refund, and shipment/tracking modeling (carrier, tracking number, delivery events) is a future domain this enum does not attempt to replace. Consumers needing interim detail can carry it in metadata.

lineItems.description: The priced rows that make up this order. At least one is required -- an order with zero line items has nothing to fulfill or bill for.

metadata.description: Freeform escape hatch for consumer-specific data this schema doesn't model. Deliberately non-interoperable -- a private extension zone, not part of the typed interop surface. Recommend reverse-DNS-style keys (e.g. "com.example.internalId") when multiple parties write to it.

number.description: Human-facing display number, e.g. shown on a packing slip or order confirmation email. NOT the system key -- this schema has no id property; consumers key orders in their own systems and reference this order however they already do internally.

placedAt.description: When the order was placed, RFC 3339.

shippingAddress.description: Delivery address for physical fulfillment. Optional -- digital/service orders may have none.

shippingTotal.description: Shipping/freight charge for the order. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the order: open (placed, not yet in progress), processing (being fulfilled/prepared), completed, or canceled. Absent means open -- the earliest lifecycle state, mirroring invoice's absent-means-draft principle: an imported order without a recorded status is treated as not-yet-progressed, never as completed.

subtotal.description: Sum of line item amounts before order-level discount, tax, and shipping adjustments. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

taxTotal.description: Total tax for the order. Optional -- see total's description for the full identity and sign convention. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

total.description: The order's grand total, authoritative regardless of whether the optional component totals are present: total = subtotal minus discountTotal plus taxTotal plus shippingTotal. This schema cannot enforce that arithmetic -- consumers compute it, and total is the source of truth for billing even if the components are absent or don't sum to it exactly. Non-negative via the sibling properties/amount/minimum, composed alongside the $ref.

title: Order
